summary: A 20-ft timber L-4 tower in the Glacier Peak Wilderness, dated 1938 by the NRHP nomination but 1953 by NHLR; volunteers staff it during fire danger.

facts.design: L-4 cabin, 14 x 14 ft with catwalk, on a 20-ft timber tower

access.note: Forest Service lists the site as open with no fee; trail access only. Active alerts for a Suiattle River Road washout and a fire closure order were listed when checked.

visit.trail_note: About a 26.5-mile round trip from the Suiattle Trailhead, reached by a 23.5-mile drive on Suiattle River Road (Forest Service). NHLR describes a 12-mile hiking trail; the nomination puts the nearest trailhead 16 miles away.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest

events.note: Firelookout.com: first developed about 1926 with a 10x10 ft shake cabin; the nomination says the site was in use by 1928
Forest Service records show a fire report from Miners Ridge; the site was in use as a lookout point

Present tower and cabin, replacing an older lookout house; built per the 1936 revised L-4 plan; builders Claude Brazelton and Hugh Ritter, possibly a CCC crew. Firelookout.com also gives 1938 for the replacement tower.
District ranger Warren Pressentin fell through the lookout floor hatch about 20 feet; the rescue helicopter crashed while landing on the ridge north of the lookout. Everyone survived.
Stairway relocated so the cabin is entered through the catwalk rather than the interior
NHLR and firelookout.com date the present tower to 1953; the nomination dates it to 1938 (see corrections)
Tom and Suzanne Brown listed as lookout personnel
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on January 20, 1994

corrections.why: The nomination and NHLR both describe a 20-foot (about 6.1 m) timber tower. No source read gives 32 m for this structure.

The NRHP nomination dates the present tower to 1938 (replacing an older house, per a 1936 plan). NHLR and firelookout.com give 1953 for the present tower, so the editor should confirm before the record changes. The 1953 date is kept as an event.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination gives about 6,210 ft on a knoll; NHLR gives 6,129 ft (1,868 m). The record's 1868.1 m matches NHLR and is kept.

Distances differ: NHLR describes a 12-mile hiking trail; the nomination says the nearest trailhead is 16 miles away; the Forest Service describes a 26.5-mile round trip from the Suiattle Trailhead. All three are reported in the story.
The nomination and firelookout.com say volunteers staff the lookout. One NHLR visitor comment says two NPS rangers do. The comment is treated as unverified and volunteers are used.

notes_for_editor: Build date conflict: the nomination (the most detailed source) dates the present tower to 1938 with a 1936 plan; NHLR and firelookout.com give 1953 for the present tower. A correction to 1938 is proposed but needs your confirmation. Height: the brief's 32.0 m is not supported by any source read; sources give 20 ft. Staffing: volunteers per nomination and firelookout.com; an NHLR visitor comment says two NPS rangers (unverified). Access: the Forest Service page was seen with active alerts for a Suiattle River Road washout and a fire closure order, with no dates; check current status before relying on the access level. Elevation differs (nomination about 6,210 ft; NHLR 6,129 ft). The only fire on record in the sources is the 1928 fire report. No photo with a usable image URL was found. The 1926 cabin date comes only from firelookout.com.
